title: Drawloom
summary: A drawloom carries a harness of cords that gather the pattern threads into groups. A helper pulls the cords for each pick while the weaver throws the shuttle, so the cloth can carry whole pictures: flowers, birds and clouds in glossy silk. It is the forerunner of the jacquard loom.
howToPlay: Pick a silk colour from the reels and a pattern shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the panel to weave that shape there; it is mirrored on the other half of the panel.
Copy the panel shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The panel is mirrored left and right, so every shape you weave is also woven on its partner square.
A square counts only when its shape and its silk colour both match the panel you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Drawlooms wove the figured silks of China and, later, of Italian and other European silk towns. A weaver and a helper had to work in step, and one metre of rich cloth could take days.
credits: Pattern design: World Heritage Games (original, in the style of the tradition)
